quote: The day loop, yes. Four things, no.
text: Four things stay with the maintainer: plan.md (writing it, changing it, lifting each stopping point), the gates (CI, hooks, CLAUDE.md, the scripts, branch protection), everything outside the repository, and parks.

quote: driver never carries a session past its own PR
text: The driver calls `claude -p` once per step, so each step is a new session with an empty context: one step, one session, one pull request, then the session stops; the driver never carries a session past its own PR and always takes a new session after a merge.

quote: the driver not running, everything works as today
text: The driver is a second, opt-in way to run the same workflow: with the driver not running, everything works as today in manual mode.

quote: What the driver adds applies only to sessions it starts
text: What the driver adds applies only to sessions it starts: it passes its hooks with `--settings` and its rules with `--append-system-prompt-file` from its own folder, nothing of it is in a project's `.claude/`, and a project needs no change to be driven.

quote: The state is in git and on GitHub, so the mode can change at any step boundary
text: The state is in git and on GitHub, so the mode can change at any step boundary: the driver can be stopped and the work continued by hand, or started in the middle of a day.

quote: at once on one repository: the driver holds a lock file while it runs and refuses to start while a manual session's branch is unmerged
text: Never both modes at once on one repository: the driver holds a lock file while it runs and refuses to start while a manual session's branch is unmerged.

quote: and the next step from the project's `scripts/spec-drift.py`, and adds only
text: The driver has a repository of its own and holds no rule of the workflow: it reads the order of a day from the project's CLAUDE.md and the next step from the project's `scripts/spec-drift.py`, and adds only the switches, the parks and the merge. No pull request in the kit is made for the driver alone.

quote: driver never drives its own repository
text: The driver's repository is built by hand one day spec at a time, and the driver never drives its own repository.

quote: A hook from the driver's settings refuses Edit and Write under the driver's folder and a shell command that names it
text: A hook from the driver's settings refuses Edit and Write under the driver's folder and a shell command that names it (level 1 refuses and detects; it does not prevent).

quote: Before each step, and at level 2 before each merge, the driver checks that its own repository is clean and at the commit it started from, and halts on a difference
text: Before each step, and at level 2 before each merge, the driver checks that its own repository is clean and at the commit it started from, and halts on a difference.

section: What the driver needs from the kit
quote: sentence the driver does not know
text: A next-step sentence the driver does not know, or anything else it does not recognise in a run, is a park, never a guess.

section: What the driver needs from the kit
quote: acts only on pull requests the maintainer's account opened, and puts no PR title or body into a prompt
text: The driver filters pull requests by author itself: it acts only on pull requests the maintainer's account opened, and puts no PR title or body into a prompt.

section: What the driver needs from the kit
quote: and the maintainer writes the day's spec by hand
text: The step "write its day spec" stays a manual hand-off for now: the driver parks on it and the maintainer writes the day's spec by hand.

section: What the driver needs from the kit
quote: that `scripts/pr-names.py` and `evidence.yml` are there
text: At `on` a preflight runs the project's `spec-drift.py`, checks the JSON fields the driver relies on and that `scripts/pr-names.py` and `evidence.yml` are there, and refuses to turn on with one line for each missing piece; it does not adapt to an older kit.

section: What the driver needs from the kit
quote: own copy of the kit's script for every sentence it can return and checks
text: A contract test in the driver's repository calls `next_step()` in its own copy of the kit's script for every sentence it can return and checks each one is known, and the driver's README names the kit commits the test has passed on.
change: The driver's copy is no longer the kit's file but a split port (spec-drift.py plus spec_drift_*.py), so a newer kit is tested by porting its next_step() change into the copy, not by bringing the copy up to the kit; a trial's record also names its project's copy's commit.

quote: refused while a manual branch is unmerged or a halt is set
text: `python run-steps.py on` makes the driver take the next step, and is refused while a manual branch is unmerged or a halt is set.

quote: its PR, then the driver exits
text: `python run-steps.py off`, or closing the run's issue from the phone, lets the current step finish its PR, then the driver exits and nothing new starts.

quote: then on a hook refuses every tool call in every session the driver started, subagents included
text: A halt writes the halt file in the driver's folder, and from then on a hook refuses every tool call in every session the driver started, subagents included; the file is a plain file, so creating it by hand works even with the driver broken.

quote: what was in progress to the run's issue: the step, the branch, the last commit
text: A halt then kills the running session and its whole process tree, merges nothing, starts nothing and exits (open pull requests stay open, nothing merged or pushed is undone), and writes what was in progress to the run's issue: the step, the branch, the last commit, and whether the tree had uncommitted changes.
change: A halt must now also kill the session's container by the name the run log gives it (docker kill), because killing the driver's process tree leaves the container running.

quote: it takes as long as the driver's poll of GitHub, 30 seconds by default, and only an issue from the maintainer's account counts
text: A halt from the PC takes effect within a second; from the phone (an issue whose title starts with `STOP`) it takes as long as the driver's poll of GitHub, 30 seconds by default, and only an issue from the maintainer's account counts.

quote: driver will not start again until the maintainer clears it
text: A halt is sticky: the driver will not start again until the maintainer clears it with `run-steps.py clear`, and it comes back in manual mode, so turning the driver on again is a separate step.

quote: and never the step's session
text: The reviewer is a new session with a fresh context, read-only, and never the step's session.

quote: fix after a red check or a reviewer's blocker
text: A fix after a red check or a reviewer's blocker resumes the step's own session (`claude -p --resume <id>`) with the failing check's lines, filtered and capped, twice at most; it does not start another session.

quote: the driver's settings refuse
text: A merge is done by the maintainer or (level 2) the driver, never by a step session: the driver's settings refuse `gh pr merge` and a push to `main`. A force-push never happens under automation; a hook refuses it.

quote: the maintainer reads them
text: At the end of a phase the plan-auditor runs on both phases by itself, and the driver parks with the report until level 3. At the end of the last phase the three auditors run by themselves and the maintainer reads them.

quote: a `Hand-off` line to the maintainer in the
text: In a driven session a lesson for CLAUDE.md is written as a `Hand-off` line to the maintainer in the day's Notes, and the maintainer lands it.

quote: `specs/README.md`, the templates, `spec-drift.config.json`
text: Kit and gate changes are human-only files that only the maintainer merges: `.github/`, `.claude/`, `scripts/`, CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, `specs/README.md`, the templates, `spec-drift.config.json`, and plan.md.

quote: A park opens an issue labelled `parked` with the reason and stops the run
text: A park opens an issue labelled `parked` with the reason and stops the run, and the driver resumes when the maintainer's account closes the issue.

quote: step session's last line is `PARK: <reason>`
text: The driver parks when the step session's last line is `PARK: <reason>`, which is how a session hands over a step it could not finish or would not decide (a frozen file, a criterion that cannot be met).

quote: or a human-only file, or carries
text: The driver parks when the pull request touches plan.md or a human-only file, or carries an `Oversized:` line.

quote: required check is still red, or the reviewer still has a blocker, after two fixes
text: The driver parks when a required check is still red, or the reviewer still has a blocker, after two fixes.

quote: failed, is missing, or did not finish
text: After a close the driver checks the evidence run on the merge commit (`gh run list`, `gh run view --exit-status`) and parks when it failed, is missing, or did not finish.

quote: next step is a stopping point, the end of a phase (levels 1 and 2), or "Every day is done."
text: The driver parks when the next step is a stopping point, the end of a phase (levels 1 and 2), or "Every day is done."

quote: or the same step failed twice
text: The driver parks when a step passed its budget or the same step failed twice.

quote: looks for the PR on GitHub by the step's branch, not in the session's text, and never hands a half-done branch to a new session
text: The driver parks when the session ended with neither a pull request nor `PARK:`; it looks for the PR on GitHub by the step's branch, not in the session's text, and never hands a half-done branch to a new session.

quote: working tree is not clean, or a clean one cannot be brought to `main` equal to `origin/main` by a switch and a fast-forward
text: Before a step, the driver parks when the project's working tree is not clean, or a clean one cannot be brought to `main` equal to `origin/main` by a switch and a fast-forward.

quote: parks, and the run log counts how often
text: When the day's audit found nothing and so no spec-change PR opens, the driver parks, and the run log counts how often.

quote: mode, and nothing falls back to `bypassPermissions`
text: A permission refusal that stopped a step is a park and the run log counts them; the sessions run in `auto` mode, the driver never changes the permission mode, and nothing falls back to `bypassPermissions`.

quote: the driver waits and retries, and parks only if that fails
text: When the usage limit is reached the driver waits and retries, and parks only if that fails.

quote: A restart must never start a second session for a step that has one, open a second pull request for it, or discard work nobody finished
text: A restart must never start a second session for a step that has one, open a second pull request for it, or discard work nobody finished.

quote: The driver decides from git and GitHub first
text: The driver decides from git and GitHub first; the run log holds only a step's session id, its count of fixes and the lock, and a lost or torn log makes the driver park, not guess.

quote: Before a session starts, the driver appends the step, its branch prefix and the session id it chose (`--session-id`) to the run log
text: Before a session starts, the driver appends the step, its branch prefix and the session id it chose (`--session-id`) to the run log and flushes the line.

quote: The lock names the driver's process and when it started
text: The lock names the driver's process and when it started: a second `on` refuses while that process lives, and a lock whose process is gone is taken over only after the start table has been read.

quote: reboot, and the answer to a park all read the
text: `on`, a restart after a crash or reboot, and the answer to a park all read the same start table from the top and act on the first row that applies (halt, live session, open parked issue, open PR, uncommitted changes, unfinished branch, clean tree elsewhere, clean `main`); nothing is carried over but the run log.
change: The start table's live-session row now also counts a running container the log names (a crashed driver leaves one), and the table is read again when the container ends.

quote: a crash the driver resumes nothing by itself: the step parks with its session id, and
text: Nothing starts a second session while a branch of the step exists, and after a crash the driver resumes nothing by itself: the step parks with its session id, and when the log cannot say how many fixes were used, both count as used.

short: Driver opens and closes no PR
quote: The driver opens no pull request and closes none
text: The driver opens no pull request and closes none: sessions open them, the driver finds them by branch, and on an open PR for the step it waits and starts nothing.

quote: Before it opens a `parked` issue the driver looks for an open one for the same step and reason, and comments there
text: Before it opens a `parked` issue the driver looks for an open one for the same step and reason, and comments there instead.

quote: `status`, `rev-parse`, `for-each-ref`, `ls-remote`, `fetch`, and on a clean tree `switch main` and `merge --ff-only`
text: The driver's git commands are only `status`, `rev-parse`, `for-each-ref`, `ls-remote`, `fetch`, and on a clean tree `switch main` and `merge --ff-only`; never `reset`, a checkout of a path, `clean`, `stash`, `branch -D`, a forced push or the deletion of a branch.
change: The closed list of the driver's git commands gained two read-only ones, symbolic-ref and ls-remote --get-url.

quote: After a reboot the driver stays off until the maintainer runs `on`
text: After a reboot the driver stays off until the maintainer runs `on`.

short: Closing a park means go on
quote: Closing a park's issue is the maintainer's "go on", not an instruction
text: Closing a park's issue is the maintainer's "go on", not an instruction: if the step was finished by hand the next step follows, if its branch was deleted the step starts again in a new session, and if the branch is still there the driver parks again.

quote: the driver exists and its `--dry-run` names the step `spec-drift.py` prints
text: Level 1 (the driver starts steps, the maintainer merges each PR) is entered when the driver exists and its `--dry-run` names the step `spec-drift.py` prints and a phase's end, with sessions in `auto` mode and a fine-grained token scoped to the trial's repository (contents, pull requests and issues; no Administration, no Workflows).

quote: 15 PRs in a row merged at level 1 without the maintainer asking for a change
text: Level 2 / Phase 2 (the driver also merges a PR that passes every gate and touches no human-only file) is entered only after 15 PRs in a row merged at level 1 without the maintainer asking for a change, with the sessions under a second Windows account with no write on the driver's folder, and `main` requiring a pull request and allowing no bypass.
change: Level 2 now needs the sessions in the driver's container (driver's folder mounted read-only) instead of a second Windows account, and the 15 PRs are counted from container sessions only, so the Day 8 trial's 3 do not count.

quote: starts the next phase when the plan-auditor names no plan change
text: Level 3 / Phase 3 (phases chain): the driver starts the next phase when the plan-auditor names no plan change; it is entered only after one whole phase at level 2 with no escape.

quote: on an escape: a Defect line found at `close`, by the `dashboard` or in a `Day NN review`, or a failed evidence replay after a merge
text: The driver goes back one level on an escape: a Defect line found at `close`, by the `dashboard` or in a `Day NN review`, or a failed evidence replay after a merge.

quote: 34.4 replies per merged pull request
text: An unattended run should not raise $1.86 per merged pull request or 34.4 replies per merged pull request, with the reviewer session counted in; beside them it is judged on escapes per day, parks by reason and refusals.

quote: first: nothing of level 2 is built until the trial at level 1 has been read
text: Level 1 is built first: nothing of level 2 is built until the trial at level 1 has been read.

quote: so an update that changes how settings merge fails a test and not a run
text: The repository's first test repeats the `--settings` check on the installed CLI (hooks from `--settings` are added to the project's), so an update that changes how settings merge fails a test and not a run.

quote: `on`, `off`, `status`, `halt`, `clear`; `--dry-run` prints the step and starts nothing; `--once` does one step
text: `run-steps.py` has the switches `on`, `off`, `status`, `halt`, `clear`; `--dry-run` prints the step and starts nothing; `--once` does one step; its config names the project's path, the human-only paths, the budget per step and the steps per night.

quote: and each day's `phase`, since the sentence never names a phase's end or the audit that follows it
text: The driver reads the project's `spec-drift.py --out` JSON, not only the sentence it prints: the next step and each day's `phase`, since the sentence never names a phase's end or the audit that follows it.

quote: no connector of the maintainer's
text: The driver runs each step in the project's folder as `claude -p "<step>"` with `--model` set to the main session's, `--output-format json`, `--max-budget-usd <n>`, `--strict-mcp-config`, `--settings` and `--append-system-prompt-file`, so no connector of the maintainer's account loads in an unwatched session.
change: The step now goes in on standard input instead of as the -p argument, --permission-mode auto is added to the command line, and from Day 10 the command runs inside the session's container rather than directly in the project's folder. From Day 11 it runs with --output-format stream-json --verbose in place of json, the result event standing for the JSON object.

quote: No driver without its stop: a test starts a step, halts, and checks the process is gone and a tool call is refused
text: No driver without its stop: a test starts a step, halts, and checks the process is gone and a tool call is refused.

quote: cost per PR beside the baseline
text: The run log has one line per step and `status` prints it: the mode, the level, the step in progress and its cost so far, steps, parks by reason, and cost per PR beside the baseline.

quote: driver's settings refuse it a git command that changes a repository and a `gh` command that is not a read
text: The reviewer's brief is in the driver's repository and reaches the session with `--agents` and `--agent`; the driver's settings refuse it a git command that changes a repository and a `gh` command that is not a read, and the driver compares HEAD, the refs, the stash and `git status` before and after it and parks on a difference.

quote: the path check against the human-only list, then `gh pr merge --match-head-commit <sha>`
text: The level 2 merge is the path check against the human-only list, then `gh pr merge --match-head-commit <sha>` on the commit the checks and the reviewer saw; whether a PR merged is read from GitHub, not from the log.

quote: gets its spec when its turn comes
text: Each phase is a series of pull requests under 400 lines, so CI stays green, and each day gets its spec when its turn comes.

quote: prints the step `spec-drift.py` prints or a park with its reason, and its tests show it ran only reads
text: Phase 0 (Days 1-2): the driver reads a project and names the next action and starts nothing; done when `python run-steps.py --dry-run` on a project prints the step `spec-drift.py` prints or a park with its reason, and its tests show it ran only reads.

quote: a project that is neither the kit nor the driver's own repository
text: Phase 1 (Days 3-8): one day of a project that is neither the kit nor the driver's own repository runs at level 1 with the maintainer only merging and answering parks; done when the trial's day closed with its evidence replay green and the record names every park and every permission refusal, and what it cost beside the baseline.

quote: plan-auditor reads the whole plan against the code, and Phase 2 is specified only once the maintainer lifts the stop
text: Day 8 (the level 1 trial's record) is a stopping point: the plan-auditor reads the whole plan against the code, and Phase 2 is specified only once the maintainer lifts the stop.

quote: is reverted in the kit or in a project
text: Removing the driver is deleting its folder and revoking its token: the halt file, the lock and the run log sit in the driver's folder uncommitted, and nothing is reverted in the kit or in a project.
change: Removal is no longer the folder and one token: it now also means revoking a second (Claude Code) token and deleting the session's image and the secrets file kept outside the repositories.

quote: Before each session the driver writes its settings file
text: Before each session the driver writes its settings file afresh into its own uncommitted state folder, naming each hook's script and the halt file by full path.

quote: every session the driver starts on the trial's project runs in
text: From Day 10 every session the driver starts on the trial's project runs in the driver's container, at level 1 too.

quote: may still run sessions on the PC, at level 1 only
text: Outside the trial driver.json may still run sessions on the PC, at level 1 only.

quote: Claude Code at the live-checked version
text: The driver runs each session's claude -p with docker run -i --rm --name <from the session's id>, from an image its repository builds with Claude Code at the live-checked version, python, git, gh and the project's test tools.

quote: what the driver mounts
text: The session reaches only what the driver mounts: the project's checkout writable; the driver's hooks, rules, settings file and state folder read-only; <state>/refusals and a Claude Code config folder writable.

quote: never on the command line, in the run log or in a mount
text: The fine-grained GitHub token and a Claude Code token reach the session only as environment variables from a file outside both repositories (--env-file), never on the command line, in the run log or in a mount.

quote: Docker socket, the maintainer's profile or
text: The Docker socket, the maintainer's profile or ~/.claude, the folder holding the repositories and the secrets file are never mounted, and the container is never --privileged.

quote: false, and the commit identity and
text: The image's /etc/gitconfig sets safe.directory to the mounted checkout, core.autocrlf true, core.filemode false, and the commit identity and credential helper the push needs.

quote: The driver kills a session with
text: The driver kills a session with docker kill, and the driver itself stays on the PC under the maintainer's account and gh login, where it polls and at level 2 merges.

quote: the session installs the project as CI does before
text: In the container the session installs the project as CI does before running its tests.

section: What the driver needs from the kit
quote: trial's record names the commit of its project's copy
text: A trial's record names the commit of its project's copy of the kit's script.

quote: read from the container's Claude Code folder
text: At a close the step sessions' transcripts are read from the container's Claude Code folder in the driver's state, and token-usage.py is pointed there.

quote: polls the required checks
text: The driver polls the required checks (gh pr checks <n> --required) every --poll seconds instead of waiting with --watch.

quote: takes its mode from the maintainer's own
text: The driver passes --permission-mode auto on every call, so a headless session never takes its mode from the maintainer's own settings.

short: Merge on only when three hold
quote: requires a pull request with no bypass
text: Phase 2's days are built at level 1, and the level 2 merge is switched on in a run, and refuses otherwise, only when status reports 15 of 15, the sessions run in the container and main requires a pull request with no bypass.

quote: the driver's guard and halt hooks log each refusal to the driver's state folder, so a killed session's refusals are counted
text: Day 9: the driver's guard and halt hooks log each refusal to the driver's state folder, so a killed session's refusals are counted.

quote: the halt tests that fail on and off, and the race they may show
text: Day 9: the halt tests that fail on and off, and the race they may show, are dealt with.

quote: level 2 count to the park sentence it counts
text: Day 9: a test ties status's level 2 count to the park sentence it counts.

quote: preflight checks that Docker runs, the image exists and its Claude Code is the live-checked version
text: Day 10: on's preflight checks that Docker runs, the image exists and its Claude Code is the live-checked version.

quote: checks from inside the container that the driver's folder cannot be written and that the project and
text: Day 10: before a session, on checks from inside the container that the driver's folder cannot be written and that the project and <state>/refusals can.

quote: the usage limit is read from the container's Claude Code folder
text: Day 10: the usage limit is read from the container's Claude Code folder.

quote: level 2 count reads only container sessions
text: Day 10: status's level 2 count reads only container sessions.

quote: reports "do not allow bypassing"
text: Day 10, in its own track: this repository's setup-check.py reports "do not allow bypassing".

quote: the check of the driver's own repository before each merge
text: Day 13's level 2 merge spec carries Replaces: C07.1 and includes the check of the driver's own repository before each merge.

quote: and the record names every merge the driver made, every park and every refusal
text: Phase 2 (Days 9-14) is done when the level 2 trial's day closed with its evidence replay green and the record names every merge the driver made, every park and every refusal, with cost beside the baseline and level 1.

quote: Day 14 (the level 2 trial's record) is a stopping point
text: Day 14 (the level 2 trial's record) is a stopping point: the plan-auditor reads the whole plan before Phase 3.

quote: `budget_usd` 10 per step and `steps_per_night` 6 in `driver.json`
text: The trial's project is bearing, with budget_usd 10 per step, steps_per_night 6 and a ten-path human-only list in driver.json.

quote: in `refusals.json` on the `dashboard-data` branch
text: The refusals it is judged on are the run log's and this repository's refusals.json on the dashboard-data branch.

section: Where am I, while a session runs
quote: the driver rewrites `<state>/heartbeat.json`
text: At each poll the driver rewrites <state>/heartbeat.json with the session, its step, when it started, the time of the poll and the time of the session's last event; it is overwritten, not appended.

section: Where am I, while a session runs
quote: on the host and written by the driver, never from inside the container
text: The driver runs claude -p with --output-format stream-json --verbose, reads its output line by line on a reader thread, and appends each event's time and kind to <state>/sessions/<session>.events.jsonl, on the host and written by the driver, never from inside the container.

section: Where am I, while a session runs
quote: The `result` event stays the record
text: The result event stays the record: cost, session id and permission_denials are read from it; a stream with no result is a session that printed nothing; a line that does not parse is counted, not fatal; the poll, STOP and --session-minutes work as before.

section: Where am I, while a session runs
quote: It prints `status` again at each poll until the session ends
text: status --watch prints status again at each poll until the session ends: the step, how long it has run, its last event and how long ago, and the tokens so far; the cost stays the result's, never estimated in dollars.

section: Where am I, while a session runs
quote: Fewer than three: no estimate
text: Beside how long the session has run, the median length of the run log's earlier sessions of the same kind, and its n; fewer than three, no estimate.

section: Where am I, while a session runs
quote: one new comment says so, once per session
text: One comment on the run's issue per session, edited in place at each poll; when no event has come for stale_minutes (10 by default, in driver.json), one new comment says so, once per session; a stale session is reported, not killed.
